card.title: Dutch
card.text: The standard Dutch of the Netherlands, from first words to C1, with 13 professional specializations.

heading: Learn Dutch from first words to C1.
lead: A complete course in the standard Dutch of the Netherlands: 76 modules in eight tiers, with the grammar explained directly, from de and het to verb clusters, the passive and nominal style. Every answer gets feedback that says why, and every Dutch word can be tapped for its meaning, forms and audio.
fineprint: The whole course is free, with the grammar reference, word practice and the placement test. Specializations, NT2 practice papers, stories, conversation practice and the other extras are part of Premium, €8.99 a month or €69.99 a year.

panel.label: The course, tier by tier

items.title: 1 · Sounds and first words
items.text: Pronunciation and spelling, greetings, de and het, zijn and numbers.

items.title: 2 · Everyday basics
items.text: The present tense, hebben and er is, plurals, word order, questions and negation.

items.title: 3 · Daily life
items.text: Modal and separable verbs, adjective endings, prepositions, food, the city and shopping.

items.title: 4 · The past
items.text: The perfect with hebben and zijn, the simple past, the imperative, travel and health.

items.title: 5 · Building fluency
items.text: Subordinate clauses, the word er, the future, te and om te, work and education.

items.title: 6 · Intermediate
items.text: Zou and conditions, relative clauses, verb clusters, the pluperfect and the passive.

items.title: 7 · Upper intermediate
items.text: The passive in all tenses, reported speech, connectors, laten, word formation and the Dutch of government letters and forms.

items.title: 8 · Advanced
items.text: Nominal style, modal particles, register, spoken Dutch, Flemish and other varieties, literature and law.

panel.note: 76 modules from A1 to C1. The placement test lets you start further up.

sections.heading: Grammar explained, practice that says why

items.title: Grammar taught directly
items.text: Each module explains its rule before you practise it: why the verb goes to the end of a subordinate clause, when an adjective takes -e, what the four uses of er are. The grammar reference keeps every explanation in one place.

items.title: Feedback with a reason
items.text: A wrong answer gets an explanation of what was wrong and a link to the rule, not just a red mark.

items.title: Every word inspectable
items.text: Tap any Dutch word in an exercise, text or explanation for its meaning, its forms and its audio.

items.title: Listening, writing and speaking
items.text: Exercises include dictation, listening, translation both ways, cloze and reading texts, and speaking exercises with pronunciation feedback.

items.title: The Dutch people actually use
items.text: The standard Dutch of the Netherlands, with modules on spoken Dutch, the Dutch of government letters and forms, and the varieties of Dutch, including Flemish.

items.title: No gamification
items.text: No streaks, points or mascots. Progress is the share of the course you have finished, and the vocabulary page shows how many words you know.

items.question: Is the Dutch course really free?
items.answer: Yes. All 76 modules from A1 to C1, the grammar reference, word practice, the placement test and 5 Ask AI questions a day are free. Premium adds the specializations, exam papers, stories, conversations and other extras.

items.question: Which Dutch does the course teach?
items.answer: The standard Dutch of the Netherlands. A module in the advanced tier covers the varieties of Dutch, including the Dutch of Flanders.

items.question: I already know some Dutch. Do I have to start at the beginning?
items.answer: No. The placement test finds your level, so you can start from the tier that fits.

items.question: Does it help with inburgering or the NT2 exam?
items.answer: The course goes from A1 to C1, past the B1 and B2 levels of the Staatsexamen NT2, and Premium has practice papers for both programmes. The papers do not cover speaking and give no pass mark; the NT2 page explains what they cover.

items.question: I speak German. Is there a course for me?
items.answer: Yes. Dutch for German speakers is a shorter course explained in German, built around what differs from German: Niederländisch für Deutschsprachige.

closing.heading: Start with the first module, or with the placement test.
closing.text: Sign in with Google, take the placement test if you already know some Dutch, and open the first module.
